value.body: A music teacher teaches singing or an instrument to children or adults. Schools hire music teachers for classes, choirs and events; music academies and private classes teach students for graded exams and performances. Days are spent planning lessons, teaching, and preparing students for shows.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BPA or B.Mus. (or a diploma from a recognised music body)

items.label: Where you work
items.value: Schools, music academies, private and online classes

items.label: Students in B.Mus. and M.Mus.
items.note: Many music students study in B.A./M.A. Music or B.P.A. programmes instead, which are counted separately
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Ministry of Education (Table 11, all modes)

items.label: Students in B.P.A. (Performing Arts)
items.note: Covers music, dance and theatre together
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Ministry of Education (Table 11, all modes)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Start by teaching at a music academy, school or through private and online classes. Government school posts (KVS, NVS, state schools) have their own eligibility rules and recruitment exams.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Teaching technique in vocal or instrumental music
Planning lessons for different ages and levels

value.title: At a glance
items: Many teachers also perform or run their own classes.
College teaching usually needs a master's plus UGC-NET or a PhD.
Online classes have widened the student base beyond your own city.

competition.note: BPA graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among BPA graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
